subsystems.name: Light source
subsystems.role: emits high-intensity broadband light pulses that are absorbed by the target material and converted to heat.

subsystems.name: Pulse power supply
subsystems.role: stores electrical energy and discharges it in controlled millisecond or microsecond pulses.

subsystems.name: Substrate transport
subsystems.role: moves the material under the lamp at a defined speed for uniform exposure.

subsystems.name: Process control and monitoring
subsystems.role: measures temperature and optical properties in real time to keep the cure within limits.

subsystems.name: Atmosphere control
subsystems.role: optionally provides an inert gas blanket to prevent oxidation during curing.

subsystems.name: Cooling system
subsystems.role: removes waste heat from lamps and reflectors to allow continuous operation.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the ink or coating
buildSteps.detail: A material such as a silver nanoparticle ink is designed to absorb the lamp spectrum and cure or sinter at temperatures well below the substrate's damage threshold.

buildSteps.title: Design the pulse profile
buildSteps.detail: Energy density (joules per square centimetre), pulse length (typically 0.1–10 ms) and number of pulses are chosen from the material's absorption and thermal limits.

buildSteps.title: Build the lamp array
buildSteps.detail: Flash lamps are mounted in a reflector housing to give uniform illumination across the width of the web or part.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the power supply
buildSteps.detail: Capacitors are charged to a set voltage and discharged through the lamps via fast switches, producing repeatable pulses.

buildSteps.title: Integrate transport and controls
buildSteps.detail: The substrate is threaded through the system, and pyrometers and reflectance sensors are calibrated to monitor the process.

buildSteps.title: Run and tune
buildSteps.detail: Trials vary pulse energy and line speed until the film reaches the required conductivity or cure without damaging the substrate.

buildSteps.title: Qualify the process
buildSteps.detail: Samples are tested for adhesion, conductivity or hardness, and the recipe is locked for production.

prerequisites.why: xenon flash lamps can deliver kilowatts per square centimetre in millisecond pulses.
capacitor banks and solid-state switches can discharge stored energy precisely.
silver and copper inks absorb light and sinter at temperatures far below their bulk melting points.
enables continuous processing of flexible substrates at high speed.
pyrometers and optical sensors allow real-time control of the cure.

pathway.milestone: commercial systems cure printed silver conductors for touch sensors and RFID antennas
pathway.unlocks: low-cost, high-speed production on plastic and paper.

pathway.milestone: scale to wider webs and faster line speeds for flexible displays and solar cells
pathway.unlocks: replacement of slow thermal curing in large-area electronics.

pathway.milestone: cure copper and other air-sensitive materials using inert atmospheres
closed-loop control with real-time metrology for 3D and multilayer structures
pathway.unlocks: reliable curing in additive manufacturing and printed devices.
